title: Notes - IDOR Note Access (Easy)
description: Access a private note belonging to the administrator by manipulating the sequential note identifier in the API request.
hints: Log in as Alice (alice / alice123) and check the note IDs in the API responses or URL when viewing your own notes.
The note IDs are sequential integers (e.g. 3, 4). The first note created on the platform (ID 1) belongs to admin and contains sensitive data.

title: Notes - IDOR Note Access (Medium)
description: Bypass encoded or obfuscated note identifiers to view the administrator's confidential note.
hints: In Medium difficulty, examine the note IDs returned by GET /api/notes. They appear to be base64-encoded strings.
Base64-encode the integer 1 (i.e. 'MQ==') and request /api/notes/MQ==, or test query parameter overrides such as /api/notes/3?note_id=1.

title: Notes - IDOR Note Access (Hard)
description: Note IDs are UUIDs, but information disclosure in public activity or user profile endpoints leaks the admin's secret note identifier.
hints: UUIDs cannot be enumerated sequentially. Look for information disclosure in other endpoints such as the audit log or user profile.
Inspect GET /api/activity or GET /api/users/admin/public-profile to locate the leaked note UUID, then request /api/notes/<UUID>.

title: Notes - Privilege Escalation to Admin (Easy)
description: Escalate privileges to administrator via mass assignment in profile settings to read the admin flag.
hints: Look at the profile update endpoint at PUT /api/users/profile.
The server does not whitelist permitted fields. Send a JSON body containing {"role": "admin"} and check your updated privileges.

title: Notes - Privilege Escalation to Admin (Medium)
description: Bypass role checks using HTTP header spoofing or method overrides to access the administrator dashboard.
hints: Mass assignment is blocked on PUT /api/users/profile. How does the admin authorization check authenticate roles?
Try sending reverse-proxy style headers like X-Role: admin or X-User-Role: admin, or HTTP method override headers like X-HTTP-Method-Override: ADMIN.

title: Notes - Privilege Escalation to Admin (Hard)
description: Abuse an IDOR in the user profile update endpoint or nested metadata to escalate privileges or modify the administrator account.
hints: Inspect the user management endpoint PUT /api/users/:id. Does it check whether you are updating your own ID or another user's ID?
Update user 1's password directly via PUT /api/users/1 with {"password": "..."}, or send nested metadata {"metadata": {"role": "admin"}}.
